findings: No sustained arrhythmia. No pauses greater than 2 seconds. No AV block.

csf.interpretation: Unremarkable CSF. Normal cell count, protein, and glucose.

ct.impression: No acute intracranial abnormality. No hemorrhage, mass, hydrocephalus or large-territory infarct.

findings: Normal sinus rhythm. Normal axis and intervals. No acute ST-T changes.
Structurally normal heart. No intracardiac thrombus or vegetation. No pericardial effusion.

signal_characteristics.T1: Reduced right hippocampal volume with loss of internal architecture

mri.impression: Right mesial temporal sclerosis, unchanged compared with the MRI of 3 years ago. No new intracranial abnormality.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Normal interictal examination, and reported semiology of the new events that differs from his documented temporal lobe seizures
action_criteria.label: Examine and document the semiology of the new events against his known seizures
action_criteria.rationale: With established epilepsy, the history of how the new events differ from his documented seizures (witness account) and a normal interictal examination guide the diagnosis, which the recording then settles (Avbersek 2010; AAN 2025).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: New-type habitual event recorded on video without ictal change, alongside persistent right temporal interictal discharges
action_criteria.label: Video-EEG to record a new-type event
action_criteria.rationale: In a patient with established right temporal lobe epilepsy, a recorded habitual new event is the surest way to separate a seizure recurrence from functional seizures; about one in five patients with functional seizures also has epilepsy (LaFrance 2013; Kutlubaev 2018; AAN 2025). Without the recording, the positive signs and the semiology of witnessed events support the diagnosis at a lower ILAE level of certainty (LaFrance 2013).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Levetiracetam mood and behavioural effects and the risk of abrupt withdrawal noted; no interaction with the diabetes medicines
action_criteria.label: Review levetiracetam and his other medicines
action_criteria.rationale: Levetiracetam continues for his epilepsy; its mood and behavioural effects matter in a distressed patient, and it must not be stopped abruptly (AAN 2025).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Profile of the comorbid symptoms that treatment will target; it does not make the diagnosis
action_criteria.label: Neuropsychological assessment of comorbidity
action_criteria.rationale: A battery with performance-validity measures can quantify his mood, anxiety and distress to plan treatment; it costs more than any other step on this pathway and adds nothing to the diagnosis, which rests on the examination.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Background reading only; no result in it changes this patient's diagnosis or plan
action_criteria.label: Literature search on FND diagnosis and treatment (background, not a clinical step)
action_criteria.rationale: General evidence on the positive diagnosis and treatment of functional neurological disorder; it is not part of this patient's diagnostic pathway and no step of the work-up depends on it.

prohibited_recommendations: Order further investigations once the positive diagnosis is established, without a new specific clinical question (repeat MRI, CT, lumbar puncture, EMG or nerve conduction studies, evoked potentials, PET).
Tell the patient the symptoms are imagined, feigned, 'all in your head', or that nothing is wrong.
Perform invasive testing without a specific indication (lumbar puncture, nerve or muscle biopsy, catheter angiography).
Add or escalate antiseizure medication for the new functional events.
Give benzodiazepines or intubate for a typical functional event.
Give gadolinium contrast without a specific indication.
Stop or taper levetiracetam because the new events are functional.
required_recommendations: Make a positive diagnosis of functional neurological disorder (functional seizures coexisting with established right temporal lobe epilepsy) based on the semiology of the new events, which differs from his known seizures, confirmed where recorded by a habitual new event on video-EEG without ictal change, and not by exclusion of other disease.
Continue levetiracetam at the current dose for the established right temporal lobe epilepsy, and do not escalate antiseizure treatment for the new functional events.

Explain the diagnosis to the patient, and with consent to the family, as a common and genuine disorder of nervous system functioning that can improve, explain how the new events differ from his epileptic seizures, and give written information.
Refer for psychological therapy by a clinician experienced in FND (CBT-informed), and assess and treat any comorbid anxiety or depression.

Give the patient, family and ward a written plan for typical events: keep safe, do not restrain, wait for the event to end, and do not give emergency benzodiazepines or intubate for a typical functional seizure; rescue medication only for an event with the semiology of his known epileptic seizures.
Advise on commercial driving under the applicable regulations given the established epilepsy and the new events, and document it.

avoided_actions.rationale: The new events are long, with eyes closed and immediate recovery, and no palpitations or syncope; an ECG answers no question.
No murmur, cardiac symptom or embolic question; echocardiography answers nothing about his events.
Events of 2-5 minutes of shaking with back arching and rapid recovery are not syncopal; rhythm monitoring answers no question.
His structural substrate (right mesial temporal sclerosis) is known from MRI and the examination is normal; a CT adds radiation and no answer.
No fever, meningism, encephalopathy or inflammatory question; a lumbar puncture is invasive and answers nothing about the new events.
His epilepsy is already localized (right temporal discharges, mesial temporal sclerosis) and he is seizure-free on treatment; PET has no question to answer.
Strength, reflexes and sensation are normal; EMG has no question to answer.
Sensation is normal; evoked potentials have no question to answer.

accepted: Functional neurological disorder — PNES superimposed on established right temporal lobe epilepsy (mixed epilepsy + PNES)

differential.diagnosis: Recurrence of known right temporal lobe epilepsy (new seizure type)
differential.key_features: His epilepsy is established and interictal right temporal discharges persist, but the habitual new event was recorded without ictal change or post-event slowing, and its semiology lacks his aura, automatisms and postictal confusion.

Hypermotor seizures can lack a scalp EEG correlate, but they are usually brief, stereotyped and arise from sleep; his events last 2-5 minutes, occur awake with eyes closed, and the posterior dominant rhythm persisted during the recorded event.

Feigning is conscious and cannot be separated from FND by examination signs; a disability claim is noted, but his wife's independent account of the new events and his distress over the loss of his licence argue against it.

key_clinical_evidence: The new events (bilateral shaking with back arching and eyes closed for 2-5 minutes, immediate recovery without confusion) differ from his documented seizures (deja vu aura, oral automatisms, postictal confusion).
The video-EEG recorded a habitual new event without ictal change or post-event slowing, while right temporal interictal discharges persisted.
Established right temporal lobe epilepsy with mesial temporal sclerosis, seizure-free on levetiracetam for 4 years with a therapeutic level, coexists with the functional seizures.
The interictal neurological examination is normal; there is no limb sign.
The suspended commercial licence and a disability claim are context; they neither make the diagnosis nor show feigning.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: A father with epilepsy does not make the new events epileptic; the semiology of the new events decides it, and a recorded habitual event confirms it.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Anchor on an epileptic etiology and pursue prolonged AED trials before confirming PNES with video-EEG

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: A stressor is supportive context, neither required nor sufficient, and an incentive does not show feigning; the semiology of the events makes the diagnosis.
red_herrings.data_point: Licence suspended, loss of income and a disability claim
red_herrings.intended_effect: Conclude that stress caused the events, or that an external incentive means they are feigned

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: About one in five patients with functional seizures also has epilepsy. Interictal discharges show the known epilepsy, not the nature of the new events; the recorded new event had no ictal change.
red_herrings.data_point: Established right temporal lobe epilepsy with mesial temporal sclerosis, and right temporal interictal discharges on the video-EEG
red_herrings.intended_effect: Attribute the new events to a recurrence of his epilepsy and escalate antiseizure treatment

findings.result: Interictal examination normal: strength 5/5, normal reflexes, sensation, coordination and gait; no functional limb sign.

Bilateral whole-body shaking with back arching and eyes closed for 2-5 minutes, with immediate recovery and no postictal confusion; different from his documented seizures (deja vu and epigastric aura, oral automatisms for 60-90 seconds, postictal confusion for 5-10 minutes).
findings.sign: Reported semiology of the new events (witness account)

clinical_assessment.impression: No motor or sensory functional sign; neurological examination otherwise normal. No event was observed. The reported semiology of the new events (eyes closed, back arching, 2-5 minutes, rapid recovery without confusion) differs from his documented seizures and is typical of functional seizures; the examination does not by itself exclude epileptic seizures.

interactions: Metformin + empagliflozin: additive glucose lowering with a low risk of hypoglycemia; empagliflozin adds volume depletion and rare euglycemic ketoacidosis.
Levetiracetam with metformin or empagliflozin: no clinically significant interaction.
general.proposed: Levetiracetam 1000 mg twice daily; Metformin 1000 mg twice daily; Empagliflozin 10 mg once daily
general.summary: No clinically significant interaction between levetiracetam and the diabetes medicines. Levetiracetam carries mood and behavioural adverse effects and must not be stopped abruptly; weekend binge drinking is a caution with metformin and empagliflozin.
warnings: Levetiracetam: irritability, aggression, low mood and anxiety are recognised adverse effects. Do not stop abruptly in established epilepsy: withdrawal can provoke seizures.
Alcohol (4-6 drinks at weekends): binge drinking raises the risk of lactic acidosis with metformin and of ketoacidosis with empagliflozin, and lowers the seizure threshold.

activating_procedures.hyperventilation: 3 minutes; no change in background and no event provoked.
activating_procedures.photic_stimulation: Normal photic driving; no photoparoxysmal response.

artifacts.description: During the event; posterior channels remained interpretable between bursts.

background.focal_slowing: Intermittent right temporal theta slowing (F8, T4/T8)
background.posterior_dominant_rhythm: 10 Hz alpha, symmetric, reactive to eye opening
background.sleep_features: Normal sleep architecture with vertex waves, sleep spindles and K-complexes

findings.frequency: Intermittent, about 6 per hour, awake and asleep, more frequent in sleep
findings.morphology: Sharp-and-slow-wave complexes with maximum at F8/T4, unchanged in character from the prior study.

Eyes closed, bilateral whole-body shaking with back arching, then immediate recovery. No ictal pattern, no evolution, no post-event slowing or attenuation; the posterior dominant rhythm was visible between bursts of movement artifact, and the right temporal interictal discharges continued unchanged before and after the event.
findings.type: Clinical event - bilateral shaking with back arching

eeg.impression: This is an ABNORMAL video-EEG due to: 1. Intermittent right anterior temporal sharp-and-slow-wave discharges, unchanged from the prior study. 2. Intermittent right temporal theta slowing. One habitual event of the new type (eyes closed, bilateral shaking with back arching, 3 minutes 12 seconds) was recorded without ictal EEG change before, during or after the event; the posterior dominant rhythm persisted during the event. No electrographic seizures.
eeg.limitations: Movement artifact during the event partially obscured the frontal and temporal channels; posterior channels remained interpretable.

labs.interpretation: HbA1c 7.1% (high) and fasting glucose 128 mg/dL (high). Levetiracetam level 34 mcg/mL, within the reference range. Remaining results within reference ranges.

Prolactin.test: Prolactin (20 minutes after a new-type event)

results.finding: Diagnosis of functional neurological disorder rests on positive clinical features such as the Hoover sign, tremor entrainment and functional seizure semiology, not on the exclusion of other disease; treatment combines explanation, physiotherapy and psychological therapy.
results.source: Espay AJ et al. JAMA Neurol 2018;75:1132-1141

results.finding: Motor signs such as the Hoover sign, hip abductor sign, drift without pronation and dragging gait have high specificity; sensory signs such as midline splitting have low specificity.
results.source: Daum C et al. J Neurol Neurosurg Psychiatry 2014;85:180-190

results.finding: Defines levels of certainty for psychogenic nonepileptic seizures; the documented level requires a typical event recorded on video-EEG without ictal EEG change.
results.source: LaFrance WC Jr et al. Epilepsia 2013;54:2005-2018

results.finding: For functional seizures: assess for co-occurring epilepsy and psychiatric disorders, taper antiseizure medication without another indication, avoid benzodiazepines, and offer psychological therapy, which is possibly effective.
CBT added to standardised medical care did not reduce dissociative seizure frequency at 12 months; several secondary outcomes favoured CBT.
results.source: Goldstein LH et al. Lancet Psychiatry 2020;7:491-505

results.finding: Specialist physiotherapy for functional motor disorder was not superior to community neurological physiotherapy on physical function at 12 months; several secondary outcomes favoured it.
results.source: Nielsen G et al. Lancet Neurol 2024;23:675-686

results.finding: About 4% of patients diagnosed with conversion symptoms since 1970 later received another diagnosis.

functional neurological disorder diagnos.summary: Guideline and trial evidence supports a positive clinical diagnosis of functional neurological disorder, video-EEG confirmation of functional seizures, tapering of unneeded antiseizure drugs and benzodiazepines, and physiotherapy and psychological treatment whose trial effects on primary outcomes were modest.

metadata.difficulty_rationale: Functional seizures in a man with established right temporal lobe epilepsy and an abnormal interictal EEG. The new events differ from his known seizures, and the video-EEG records one without ictal change. The agent must diagnose the dual condition, keep levetiracetam for the epilepsy without escalating it, and address commercial driving, despite a disability claim and a suspended licence.
metadata.notes: Moderate FND — PNES superimposed on established right TLE. Classic mixed epilepsy + PNES. Video-EEG is the most informative study in a patient with known epilepsy.
metadata.revision_reason: October 2026 review round: criteria, outputs and assessment rebuilt to the FND criteria pack tiers with the dual-diagnosis variants. Close-out 24 Oct 2026: video-EEG optional and red-flag tests recommended, per the July 2026 agreement with the physicians that the examination is the only required diagnostic act.

patient.chief_complaint: New seizure-like episodes over the past 2 months — different from prior epileptic seizures

medications.indication: Type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular risk reduction

past_medical_history: Well-controlled focal epilepsy (right temporal, on levetiracetam — last seizure 4 years ago)

social_history.occupation: Truck driver (currently suspended pending medical clearance)
social_history.recent_stressor: Driver's license suspended due to new seizure events — loss of livelihood and ability to care for family

patient.history_present_illness: Mr. F is a 42-year-old truck driver with established right temporal lobe epilepsy, seizure-free on levetiracetam for 4 years, who presents with 2-month history of new episodes that he and his wife describe as different from his prior seizures. His prior epileptic seizures consisted of right temporal aura (déjà vu, rising epigastric sensation), followed by unresponsiveness with oral automatisms (lip smacking, swallowing) lasting 60-90 seconds, and post-ictal confusion for 5-10 minutes. The new episodes are distinctly different: they consist of bilateral whole-body shaking with arched back (opisthotonus-like posturing), closed eyes, 2-5 minute duration, no post-ictal confusion, and immediate full recovery. His wife is convinced these are different from his prior seizures. His driving license was suspended when he reported new episodes, creating significant financial and psychological stress as trucking is his sole income source. He has applied for disability benefits and is desperate for an explanation of the episodes. Levetiracetam level was checked by his PCP and was therapeutic. He has been compliant with medications. Prior MRI from 3 years ago showed right mesial temporal sclerosis (MTS). His diabetes is well-controlled. He has had no episodes of this kind before.

neurological_exam.additional: Interictal examination is normal. The new episodes described by the patient and his wife differ in semiology from his prior documented epileptic seizures (bilateral whole-body shaking with arched-back posturing and closed eyes, no post-ictal confusion, vs his prior right temporal aura with oral automatisms and post-ictal confusion).
neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and oriented x4. Angry and frustrated. Highly motivated to have organic explanation.
